summary: The law gives $288 ($24 a month for 12 months), which matches the engine. The household is the pregnant head alone. Countable income is $1,083.33 a month in wages plus $1,000 a month of financial assistance. Educational assistance is exempt under TWH A-1322.1. Gross income of $2,083.33 is above the 130% FPL limit but within Texas's 165% FPIL expanded categorical eligibility limit, and $190 in assets is under the TANF-NC limit, so the gross and net income tests are waived. Net income of $1,657.67 gives a formula benefit of $0 ($298 − $498), so an eligible one-person household gets the minimum benefit: 8% of $298, rounded to $24. The engine follows each of these steps and keeps the FY2026 amounts for October–December, which is right because the FY2027 COLA values came out after the 2026-07-03 freeze. The 33 models that answered $0 applied the 130% gross income test or the net income test, both of which categorical eligibility waives. The 3 that answered $1,208 dropped the $12,000 of financial assistance, which SNAP counts as income.
